meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the CWT-V1 unit
meta.scope: The cooling water system of the CWT-V1 OTS: from the CW return at the users' battery limit through FCV-201, the riser header, risers and the three induced-draft cells E-201/202/203 (fans P-212/213/214), the basin T-201 with make-up LCV-201, the circulating pumps P-215…P-218 and the supply header back to the battery limit, with the blowdown FV-222, the side-stream filter S-281 and backwash, the chemical dosing (acid, caustic, chlorine, biocide) and the utility connections at their valves (power, instrument air, city water).
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: The system is operated by trained staff at the design point (340 m³/h, return 49.2 °C, supply 32.3 °C at 27 °C wet bulb, basin 90 %). Power, instrument air and city water are available at start-up. The users' exchangers are lumped into one; their process side may be at the higher pressure. Trips LSLL-201 and VSHH-212/213/214 are proof-tested on the maintenance plan.
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

N1.causes:
FCV-201 closed (FIC-201 in MAN at 0 % or a wrong set point)
users' isolation valves shut
all circulating pumps stopped
N1.cons: Users lose cooling: process outlets rise past 47 °C and the plant must cut rate; pumps running against a closed path heat up (deadhead)

N1.causes:
one circulating pump trips
FCV-201 sticks
risers partly closed
users' valves throttled
N1.cons: Return warmer, range larger, users' outlets warmer; TI-201 can pass 55 °C (salts deposit on hot surfaces)

N1.causes:
FIC-201 set point too high
FCV-201 opens on instrument-air failure (fails open)
fourth pump started
N1.cons: More pump power; higher L/G on each cell so the supply warms a little; header pressures fall

N1.causes:
users' heat load higher than design
circulation low
a users' cooler bypassed
N1.cons: Scale and deposits in the users' hot tubes; more evaporation and drift; fill damage above about 55 °C (PVC fill)

N1.dev: Process fluid in the cooling water (users' tube leak)
N1.causes:
tube or tube-sheet leak in a users' exchanger with the process side at higher pressure
corrosion
N1.cons: Hydrocarbon carried to the cells and stripped by the fans: flammable vapour at the deck, cell fire; toxic process fluid in the drift; oil fouls the fill and the users
N1.notes:
Worked example
LOPA (worked example): values from the OTS LOPA tab, scenario L3, and teaching defaults. No existing layer is independent and able to stop the scenario: the FI-202 / FIC-201 comparison sees only an out-leak and the laboratory sample is too slow, so neither is credited. The OTS LOPA tab uses a TMEL of 1e-05 /y for severity 5; PHA Studio's teaching default is 1e-06 /y, so the gap is larger here. R04 (ASHH-201 hydrocarbon high-high stops the fans, SIL 1, PFD 0.1) closes the OTS-tab gap but not the PHA Studio one: the team must add a second layer or change the design (R05).

ie.d: Tube leak in a users' cooler with the process side at the higher pressure (0.01 /yr screening value, OTS LOPA tab scenario L3)

en.d: Process side above the CW pressure (assumed design; R05 asks the team to check it)

cm.d: A flammable cloud reaches the fan deck (consequence screening: only a larger leak is flammable; LOPA tab L3)
Ignition by the fan motors or lights (not rated for a hazardous area, HAZID H16; assumed)
A person on the fan deck (rounds and maintenance; assumed)

N1.causes:
FCV-201 closed quickly with pumps running
water hammer after a restart
N1.cons: Pressure surge on the users' exchangers and joints: leaks, a burst flexible joint

N1.dev: Process fluid flows back into the CW return
N1.causes: CW pressure lost (all pumps stopped) while a users' exchanger tube leaks
N1.cons: Process fluid fills part of the CW return: on restart it goes to the tower (as the AS WELL AS row)

sg.text: FI-202 against FIC-201 shows a water loss when the CW side leaks out (not an in-leak)
Pump curve limits the pressure to about 503 kPa g at shut-off
Restart procedure: check the return for hydrocarbon before starting the fans

recs.text: Auto-start the spare circulating pump on low supply pressure (PI-202) and add an auto-restart sequence after a power dip; the users lose cooling within minutes when all pumps stop.
Agree with the users the time they can run without cooling water and their own trips; record it as the process safety time of loss of circulation (LOPA).
Keep TI-201 under 55 °C: limit the users' load or start the spare pump when TI-201 HI alarms; write it into the operating instructions.
Install a hydrocarbon (LEL or oil-in-water) monitor on the CW return with an alarm and a high-high trip of the fans (ASHH-201).
Review the area classification of the fan deck and the fan motors for a credible hydrocarbon in-leak; specify the exchangers so the process side is at the lower pressure where possible.
Restart the pumps slowly onto drained headers (one pump, FCV-201 partly closed) to avoid water hammer; consider a surge analysis.
Before restarting the fans after a stop, sample the CW return for hydrocarbons.
